```{r}

# ==============================================================================
# I. CONFIGURATION
# ==============================================================================
BASE_DIR       <- "/home/mattia/Thesis/111125ST_def/binned_data"
SPATIAL_DIR    <- file.path(BASE_DIR, "binned_outputs/square_002um/spatial")
MATRIX_DIR     <- file.path(BASE_DIR, "binned_outputs/square_002um/filtered_feature_bc_matrix")

GEOJSON_FILE   <- file.path(BASE_DIR, "tissue_hires_image.geojson")
POSITIONS_FILE <- file.path(SPATIAL_DIR, "tissue_positions.parquet")

# ==============================================================================
# II. LOAD BINS & INVERT AXES
# ==============================================================================
message("Loading and inverting bin coordinates...")
bins_dt <- arrow::read_parquet(POSITIONS_FILE)
setDT(bins_dt) # Explicitly convert to data.table for the := operator

# Calculate midpoints for the inversion
x_mid <- (max(bins_dt$pxl_col_in_fullres) + min(bins_dt$pxl_col_in_fullres)) / 2
y_mid <- (max(bins_dt$pxl_row_in_fullres) + min(bins_dt$pxl_row_in_fullres)) / 2

# Perform the inversion (Flips the tissue orientation)
bins_dt[, pxl_col_in_fullres := x_mid - (pxl_col_in_fullres - x_mid)]
bins_dt[, pxl_row_in_fullres := y_mid - (pxl_row_in_fullres - y_mid)]

# Convert to sf object for spatial plotting
bins_sf <- st_as_sf(bins_dt, coords = c("pxl_col_in_fullres", "pxl_row_in_fullres"), remove = FALSE)
st_crs(bins_sf) <- NA

# ==============================================================================
# III. ALIGNMENT PARAMETERS (THE "TRANSFORMATION")
# ==============================================================================
# 1. Scale: Use this to grow/shrink the mask. 1.0 = original GeoJSON size.
manual_scale <- 0.305 

# 2. Rotation: Degrees (positive = counter-clockwise)
angle_deg    <- 0 
angle_rad    <- angle_deg * (pi / 180)

# 3. Nudge: Small pixel adjustments to snap the mask onto the heatmap
x_nudge      <- 539.5  
y_nudge      <- 35.25 

# Create Rotation Matrix
R_mat <- matrix(c(cos(angle_rad), -sin(angle_rad), 
                  sin(angle_rad),  cos(angle_rad)), 2, 2)

# ==============================================================================
# IV. TRANSFORM MASK (AUTO-CENTERING LOGIC)
# ==============================================================================
mask_sf <- st_read(GEOJSON_FILE)
st_crs(mask_sf) <- NA

# Step 1: Move mask to local origin (0,0) so scaling and rotation happen around its center
mask_centroid <- st_coordinates(st_centroid(st_union(mask_sf)))
st_geometry(mask_sf) <- st_geometry(mask_sf) - c(mask_centroid[1], mask_centroid[2])

# Step 2: Apply Scaling and Rotation
st_geometry(mask_sf) <- st_geometry(mask_sf) * manual_scale * R_mat

# Step 3: Shift mask to the center of the inverted bins + your manual nudge
st_geometry(mask_sf) <- st_geometry(mask_sf) + (c(x_mid, y_mid) + c(x_nudge, y_nudge))

# ==============================================================================
# IV.5 SPATIAL JOIN (CRITICAL: DO THIS BEFORE VISUALIZATION TRANSFORMS)
# ==============================================================================
# Performing the join here ensures the mask and bins are in the same 'tissue space'
message("Performing spatial join for 2um bins...")

# Disable S2 for planar data
old_s2 <- sf_use_s2()
sf_use_s2(FALSE)

# Repair mask if needed
mask_sf <- st_make_valid(mask_sf)

# Perform the join
final_assignment <- st_join(bins_sf, mask_sf, join = st_intersects, left = FALSE)

# Restore S2
sf_use_s2(old_s2)

# Create lookup table
lookup_table <- as.data.table(final_assignment)[, .(barcode, id, pxl_col_in_fullres, pxl_row_in_fullres)]
fwrite(lookup_table, file.path(BASE_DIR, "final_polygon_to_bin_lookup.csv"))
message(paste("Lookup table exported. Bins assigned:", nrow(lookup_table)))

# ==============================================================================
# V. VERIFICATION PLOT (UMI DENSITY)
# ==============================================================================
message("Reading matrix and generating heatmap...")

# Load UMIs to show the actual tissue structure
matrix_mtx <- Matrix::readMM(file.path(MATRIX_DIR, "matrix.mtx.gz"))
if(!inherits(matrix_mtx, "dgCMatrix")) matrix_mtx <- as(matrix_mtx, "dgCMatrix")

barcodes   <- fread(file.path(MATRIX_DIR, "barcodes.tsv.gz"), header = FALSE)$V1
umi_counts <- data.table(barcode = barcodes, total_umi = Matrix::colSums(matrix_mtx))
rm(matrix_mtx); gc() # Free RAM immediately

# Sample bins (1 in 20) to keep the plot responsive in WSL
plot_data <- merge(as.data.table(bins_sf), umi_counts, by = "barcode", all.x = TRUE) %>%
  .[seq(1, .N, by = 20)] %>% 
  st_as_sf(coords = c("pxl_col_in_fullres", "pxl_row_in_fullres"))

diag_plot <- ggplot() +
  # The Tissue "Heatmap"
  geom_sf(data = plot_data, aes(color = log1p(total_umi)), size = 0.01) +
  scale_color_viridis_c(option = "magma", name = "log(UMI)") +
  
  # The Candidate Mask
  geom_sf(data = mask_sf, color = "cyan", fill = "cyan", alpha = 0.15, linewidth = 0.4) +
  
  coord_sf(datum = NA) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "black"), 
        plot.background = element_rect(fill = "black"),
        panel.grid = element_blank(),
        text = element_text(color = "white")) +
  labs(title = "Alignment Verification: Inverted Bins vs. Mask",
       subtitle = "Cyan: Your Polygons | Magma: UMI Density (Tissue)")

print(diag_plot)
ggsave(file.path(BASE_DIR, "verification_plot.png"), diag_plot, width = 10, height = 10)
```

```{r}
# ==============================================================================
# PART 1: IMAGE HANDLING & MANUAL TRIM
# ==============================================================================
library(tiff)
library(grid)
library(jsonlite)
library(sf)

# 1. --- MANUAL TRIMMING CONFIGURATION (Pixels) ---
t_top <- 652; t_bottom <- 616; t_left <- 255; t_right <- 1215  

# 2. Load Native TIFF
img_raw <- readTIFF(file.path(SPATIAL_DIR, "cytassist_image.tif"), as.is = TRUE)
if (is.list(img_raw)) img <- img_raw[[1]] else img <- img_raw
if (max(img, na.rm = TRUE) > 1) img <- img / max(img, na.rm = TRUE)

# 3. Apply the Trim
img_cropped <- img[(1 + t_top):(nrow(img) - t_bottom), (1 + t_left):(ncol(img) - t_right), ]

# 4. Scale Calculations (Robust extraction)
ca_scale <- tryCatch({
  s <- as.numeric(scales$tissue_cytassist_scalef[[1]])
  if(length(s) == 0 || is.na(s)) 1 else s
}, error = function(e) 1)

# Fullres dimensions of the CROPPED area
img_w_crop <- ncol(img_cropped) / ca_scale
img_h_crop <- nrow(img_cropped) / ca_scale

# The center of your crop relative to the original image (Fullres units)
# This point is our "0,0"
center_x_orig <- (t_left + (ncol(img) - t_right)) / 2 / ca_scale
center_y_orig <- (t_top + (nrow(img) - t_bottom)) / 2 / ca_scale

# 5. Flip Image Pixels (Y-axis)
img_flipped <- img_cropped[nrow(img_cropped):1, , ]
g_img <- rasterGrob(img_flipped, width = unit(1, "npc"), height = unit(1, "npc"))

# ==============================================================================
# PART 2: MASK TRANSFORMATION (Translate -> Flip Signs -> Translate)
# ==============================================================================
# Use sf's built-in affine transformation math for robustness. 
# This avoids manual loops that can break internal matrix classes.
center_orig <- c(center_x_orig, center_y_orig)
plot_offset <- c(img_w_crop / 2, img_h_crop / 2)

# Sequence: Center -> Flip -> Offset
st_geometry(mask_sf) <- (st_geometry(mask_sf) - center_orig) * -1 + plot_offset

# ==============================================================================
# PART 3: FINAL PLOT
# ==============================================================================
diag_plot <- ggplot() +
  annotation_custom(g_img, xmin = 0, xmax = img_w_crop, ymin = 0, ymax = img_h_crop) +
  geom_sf(data = mask_sf, color = "cyan", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.5) +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(0, img_w_crop), ylim = c(0, img_h_crop), expand = FALSE, datum = NA) +
  theme_void() + 
  theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "black"), 
        plot.background = element_rect(fill = "black"))

print(diag_plot)
```

# Save the ggplot object

```{r}
# ==============================================================================
# 1. LOAD DATA & LOOKUP TABLE
# ==============================================================================
# Load the full sparse matrix (if not already in memory)
counts <- Seurat::Read10X_h5(file.path(BASE_DIR, "binned_outputs/square_002um/filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5"))

# Load the lookup table created in the previous step
lookup_table <- fread(file.path(BASE_DIR, "final_polygon_to_bin_lookup.csv"))
lookup_table <- lookup_table[!is.na(id)] # Keep only bins assigned to a polygon

# ==============================================================================
# 2. AGGREGATE COUNTS BY POLYGON ID
# ==============================================================================
message("Aggregating 2um bins into polygons...")

# Ensure barcodes match the matrix columns
valid_barcodes <- intersect(lookup_table$barcode, colnames(counts))
lookup_table <- lookup_table[barcode %in% valid_barcodes]

# Create a sparse mapping matrix (Bins x Polygons)
# This is a mathematically efficient way to sum columns by group
bin_idx <- match(lookup_table$barcode, colnames(counts))
poly_factor <- as.factor(lookup_table$id)
poly_idx <- as.numeric(poly_factor)

mapper <- sparseMatrix(
  i = bin_idx,
  j = poly_idx,
  x = 1,
  dims = c(ncol(counts), nlevels(poly_factor))
)

# Perform the aggregation: Genes x Polygons
agg_matrix <- counts %*% mapper
colnames(agg_matrix) <- levels(poly_factor)

# ==============================================================================
# 3. SEURAT PROCESSING & UMAP
# ==============================================================================
message("Creating Seurat object and running UMAP...")

# Create the object (now each 'cell' is one of your polygons)
poly_seurat <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = agg_matrix, project = "Segmented_Polygons")

# Standard Single-Cell Pipeline
poly_seurat <- poly_seurat %>%
  NormalizeData() %>%
  FindVariableFeatures() %>%
  ScaleData() %>%
  RunPCA() %>%
  FindNeighbors(dims = 1:20) %>%
  FindClusters(resolution = 0.8) %>%
  RunUMAP(dims = 1:20)

# ==============================================================================
# 4. VISUALIZATION
# ==============================================================================

# Plot 1: UMAP
p1 <- DimPlot(poly_seurat, reduction = "umap", label = TRUE) + 
  ggtitle("UMAP of Segmented Polygons")

# Plot 2: Spatial Cluster Map
# Link clusters back to spatial coordinates for a final check
cluster_data <- data.frame(
  id = colnames(poly_seurat),
  cluster = Idents(poly_seurat)
)

# Join cluster info back to the mask for plotting
mask_with_clusters <- mask_sf %>% left_join(cluster_data, by = "id")

# 1. Define the plot object
p2 <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = mask_with_clusters, aes(fill = cluster), color = "white", size = 0.1) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d() +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Spatial Distribution of Clusters")

# 2. Save the file to your working directory
# Using a wide 'width' and shorter 'height' forces a horizontal perspective
ggsave(
  filename = file.path(BASE_DIR, "anterior_midgut_plot.png"), 
  plot = p2, 
  width = 12,       # Increases horizontal space
  height = 6,       # Keeps it from being too tall
  units = "in", 
  dpi = 300         # High resolution for zooming in on your PC
)

print(p1)
print(p2)

# Save the object
saveRDS(poly_seurat, file.path(BASE_DIR, "segmented_polygons_seurat.rds"))
```

```{r}
seurat_object <- readRDS("/home/mattia/Thesis/Single-cell/seurat_ctrl_with_metadata.rds")

# FILTER: Keep only polygons with at least 1 count (ideally more)
# SCTransform usually needs a minimum of ~50-100 counts to be stable
SCT_seurat <- subset(poly_seurat, subset = nCount_RNA > 0)

# 1. Re-normalize your Spatial Polygon Object with SCT
SCT_seurat <- SCTransform(SCT_seurat, verbose = TRUE)

# 2. Ensure your SC Reference is also SCT-normalized
seurat_object <- SCTransform(seurat_object) 

# 3. Find Anchors using SCT
anchors <- FindTransferAnchors(
  reference = seurat_object,
  query = SCT_seurat,
  normalization.method = "SCT",
  reference.assay = "SCT",
  query.assay = "SCT",
  dims = 1:20
)

# 4. Transfer the Labels
predictions <- TransferData(
  anchorset = anchors,
  refdata = seurat_object@meta.data[["celltype"]], # Ensure this column name exists in sc_reference
  prediction.assay = TRUE,
  weight.reduction = SCT_seurat[["pca"]],
  dims = 1:20
)

# Add scores back to the Seurat object
SCT_seurat[["predictions"]] <- CreateAssayObject(data = predictions@data)
```

```{r}
# 1. Get the prediction scores matrix
# This assumes your predictions are in an assay called 'predictions'
prob_matrix <- GetAssayData(SCT_seurat, assay = "predictions", layer = "data")

# 2. Find the index of the max score for each column (polygon)
# We exclude the 'max' and 'prediction.score.max' rows if they exist
type_rows <- rownames(prob_matrix)[!grepl("max", rownames(prob_matrix))]
clean_matrix <- prob_matrix[type_rows, ]

# 3. Identify the most likely cell type per ID
max_type <- apply(clean_matrix, 2, function(x) type_rows[which.max(x)])

# 4. Create a lookup dataframe
winning_types <- data.frame(
  id = names(max_type),
  top_celltype = max_type,
  confidence = apply(clean_matrix, 2, max) # Optional: keep the score for transparency
)
```

```{r}
# Join the winning type to your spatial mask
mask_with_winners <- mask_with_clusters %>%
  left_join(winning_types, by = "id")

# Plot the categorical map
p_final <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = mask_with_winners, aes(fill = top_celltype), color = "white", size = 0.05) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set3", name = "Predicted Type") + # Better for discrete types
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Predicted Cell Type") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

# Save as a horizontal high-res image to maintain organization
ggsave(file.path(BASE_DIR, "most_likely_celltypes.png"), p_final, width = 14, height = 6, dpi = 300)
```

ggplot(mask_with_winners, aes(x = x_pos, fill = top_celltype)) +

  theme_minimal() +

```{r}
# Divide the gut into 10 longitudinal bins
mask_with_winners <- mask_with_winners %>%
  mutate(bin = ntile(x_pos, 10))

full_length_summary <- mask_with_winners %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  group_by(bin, top_celltype) %>%
  tally() %>%
  group_by(bin) %>%
  mutate(pct = (n / sum(n)) * 100) %>%
  # Reshape for a clean table
  tidyr::pivot_wider(id_cols = bin, names_from = top_celltype, values_from = pct, values_fill = 0)

print(full_length_summary)
```

```{r}
# 1. Identify the ISC row name
isc_row <- "ISC" # Ensure this matches your sc_reference exactly

# 2. Extract scores as a named vector
isc_probs <- SCT_seurat[["predictions"]]@data[isc_row, ]

# 3. Create a lookup table
isc_lookup <- data.frame(
  id = names(isc_probs), 
  isc_score = as.numeric(isc_probs)
)

# 4. Join to your sf object using the 'id' column
mask_with_winners <- mask_with_winners %>%
  left_join(isc_lookup, by = "id")

# 5. Handle any polygons that didn't have a score (the filtered ones)
mask_with_winners$isc_score[is.na(mask_with_winners$isc_score)] <- 0
```

```{r}
isc_summary_table <- mask_with_winners %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  group_by(cluster) %>% # Using your anatomical clusters
  summarise(
    Mean_ISC_Score = mean(isc_score, na.rm = TRUE),
    Total_Polygons = n(),
    High_Confidence_Count = sum(isc_score > 0.5, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  mutate(ISC_Density_Ratio = High_Confidence_Count / Total_Polygons) %>%
  arrange(desc(Mean_ISC_Score))

print(isc_summary_table)
```
